claims.paraphrase: The manufacturer is required by the specification to identify and document known and foreseeable hazards in normal and fault conditions with respect to the intended use.
claims.doesNotEstablish: That an assessor has found every possible hazard or that a particular manufacturer is compliant.

claims.paraphrase: The manufacturer is required to implement relevant allocated controls and to verify their implementation and effectiveness within the conditions stated by the specification.
claims.doesNotEstablish: That every proposed control is automatically effective in a different local deployment.

claims.paraphrase: The health organisation is required to define clinical scope, intended use, operational environment and intended users of the system being deployed.
claims.doesNotEstablish: That a generic supplier description fully specifies the local workflow.

claims.paraphrase: The health organisation is required to document known and foreseeable patient hazards for introduction and use, in normal and fault conditions.
claims.doesNotEstablish: That the system or our review can certify hazard completeness.

claims.paraphrase: The deploying health organisation is required to implement its risk controls and verify their implementation and effectiveness.
claims.doesNotEstablish: That a signed SOP or claim of clinician sign-off is sufficient clinical effectiveness evidence.

claims.paraphrase: The specification requires a maintained hazard log and lifecycle safety case reports with the stipulated CSO approval.
claims.doesNotEstablish: That CSO approval to a document is the same as separate organisational deployment authority.

claims.paraphrase: During procurement, the health organisation is required under the specification to ensure manufacturer/system DCB0129 compliance, with relevant supplier safety case reports available for local analysis.
claims.doesNotEstablish: That a supplier safety summary substitutes for local DCB0160 assessment.

claims.paraphrase: The health organisation must review safety concerns and changes for continuing validity of the safety case and manage safety-related modifications.
claims.doesNotEstablish: That incident reporting alone demonstrates mitigation effectiveness.

claims.paraphrase: The guidance frames healthcare ML safety as a whole-system issue involving technology, healthcare professionals and information, and presents multiple hazard-analysis techniques.
claims.doesNotEstablish: That SHARD, FRAM, SWIFT or any named technique is mandated for every deployment.

claims.paraphrase: High aggregate model performance does not establish safety for important rare conditions and intended clinical use without appropriate case-specific performance measures.
claims.doesNotEstablish: That any particular AI's high accuracy metric is inaccurate or that a fixed sensitivity threshold is universally required.

claims.paraphrase: 37.3% of 398 logged AVT uses required accuracy edits; the report lists 126 clinical-information, 43 language and 24 invented-information editing reasons.
claims.doesNotEstablish: A disjoint sum of error categories, clinical injury incidence, signed-note harm rates, or sensitivity of clinician review.

claims.paraphrase: The report identifies non-randomised, uncontrolled, self-reported and heterogeneous evaluation limitations and does not offer direct patient outcomes or systematic error tracking.
claims.doesNotEstablish: That its edit numbers can quantify patient injury risk or control effectiveness at another Trust.

claims.paraphrase: Clinicians interviewed in the GOSH multicentre AVT evaluation reported concerns about misattribution, explicit negative findings and loss of important detail through summarisation.
claims.doesNotEstablish: Frequency of each error subtype, independently confirmed injury incidents, or demonstrated local control failure.

claims.locator: second interim: summary about 180-day worklist behaviour
claims.paraphrase: The HSSIB publisher reports that e-RS entries may leave provider worklists after 180 days without action, potentially without staff recognition.
claims.doesNotEstablish: An AVT incident, transferability to another product without matching workflow, or original local risk acceptance circumstances.

claims.paraphrase: The NHS England ambient scribing guidance summary advises deploying organisations to assign CSO responsibility and complete relevant DCB0160 documentation and a DPIA.
claims.doesNotEstablish: Precise current wording or all legal consequences without full-document verification.

claims.locator: Why the standards were introduced; Rationale for review
claims.paraphrase: NHS England lists DCB0129 v4.2/DCB0160 v3.2 as current in June 2026 and describes consultation concerns about AI governance and complex system interactions.
claims.doesNotEstablish: That the consultation has replaced either published standard or that we can decide a statutory breach.
